new.basis: distinct ASNs announcing the /24s of the addresses in each vendor's published server list; the Windscribe figures count primary addresses only
new.comparison: Mullvad VPN has more ASNs than NordVPN (27 against 25) and fewer than Windscribe (27 against 58)

windscribe.servers: unverified: the 2026-10-24 table gives 1074 under servers for this vendor, and the vendor's list carries ip2 and ip3 addresses beside the primary one, so 1074 is not shown to be a count of servers

evidence.proved: How the 2026-10-24 measurement counted ASNs: each vendor's own machine-readable server list, every distinct /24 in it resolved to an ASN through RIPE, and the Windscribe count rechecked on primary addresses only (58 ASNs on 239 /24s).
evidence.quote: Each vendor's own machine-readable server list ... Every distinct /24 in that list resolved to an ASN with RIPE ... Headline numbers, all measured 2026-10-24 ... the count survives a primary-IP-only recount (58 on 239 /24s, not an artefact of the ip2/ip3 fields)

reason: the comparison of ASN counts across vendors sits in a clause of notes that the public data withholds in part; it gets a field of its own, extras.asn_comparison, because the schema has no typed field for a comparison of vendors

evidence.proved: The 2026-10-24 table lists servers, /24s and ASNs per vendor: Windscribe 1074, 239 and 58; Mullvad 566, 258 and 27; NordVPN 7193, 775 and 25. Mullvad's 27 ASNs are more than NordVPN's 25 and fewer than Windscribe's 58.
